subject: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations

messages.author: e7014f74b5d49111
messages.subject: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
parts:
I have 1 tree that I would like to display in 6 facets with annotations. The sets of annotations are coded by a variable in the dataframe that I have attached to the tree using the %<+% operator. 

e.g., I have a dataframe 'df' with the following columns (tip.names, sites, value)

I would like to call something like the following:
p <- ggtree(tree) %<+% df
p + facet_wrap(~sites) + geom_tippoint(value)

Is there a way I can produce this graphic?

messages.author: f0dc0fdb872722c6
messages.subject: Re: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
parts:
p + facet_wrap(~sites) + geom_tippoint(aes(value))

This is not meaningful for phylogenetic tree, since facet_wrap(~sites) will split the data by ~sites and plot each sub-dataset in subpanel, while all the sub-datasets don't contain a whole tree structure.


It's only possible if we duplicate the underlying data and modify the ~sites column for subset while adding an additional column for facet.

Here is an example:

library(ggtree)
nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="ggtree")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
p <- ggtree(tree)

dd <- data.frame(taxa  = LETTERS[1:13],
                 place = c(rep("GZ", 5), rep("HK", 3), rep("CZ", 4), NA),
                 value = round(abs(rnorm(13, mean=70, sd=10)), digits=1))

place <- c("CZ", "GZ", "HK")

p = ggtree(tree) %<+% dd
p$data <- lapply(place, function(x) {
    d <- p$data
    d$site <- x
    d$place[d$place != x] = NA
    d
}) %>% do.call('rbind', .)

p + facet_wrap(~site) + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=!is.na(place)))

messages.subject: Re: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
parts: another solution is to produce separate figures and use multiplot to visualize them.

p1 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "CZ")))
p2 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "GZ")))
p3 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "HK")))
multiplot(p1, p2, p3, ncol=3, labels=c("CZ", "GZ", "HK"))
